title: LeBron Walked Away From $15 Million Of Burgers

beats.say: A basketball star reportedly walked away from fifteen million dollars of burger money.
beats.visual: a single glossy burger on a paper tray on a bright white diner counter in warm morning daylight, high key lighting, shallow depth of field, no people, no text

beats.say: In twenty fifteen LeBron James let his McDonald's deal lapse. According to Forbes, his partner said that meant about fourteen to fifteen million dollars over four years.
beats.visual: a stack of crisp hundred dollar bills sliding off the edge of a steel kitchen counter, motion blur, cold overhead light

beats.say: Why say no to that? Because he had picked a different kind of payment.
beats.visual: a lone figure standing at a fork in a wet city street at dusk, two glowing paths, silhouette only

beats.say: Three years earlier, he put about one million dollars of his own money into a small pizza chain called Blaze.
beats.visual: a wood fired pizza oven glowing orange inside a modern restaurant kitchen at night, no people

beats.say: Reports say that bought him more than ten percent of the company.
beats.visual: a single pizza slice being lifted from a round pie, a long string of melted cheese, warm dramatic light

beats.say: Here is the part nobody tells you. A paycheck pays once. A piece of a company keeps growing while you sleep.
beats.visual: a green seedling pushing through cracked asphalt beside a locked steel safe, dawn light

beats.say: So he stopped selling his name for a fee and started trading it for ownership.
beats.visual: a heavy brass key turning in an old iron lock on a tall wooden door, warm backlight

beats.say: Forbes estimated his Blaze stake at about thirty million dollars in twenty twenty two.
beats.visual: a tall stack of gold coins rising beside a small stack on a black marble table, dramatic side light

beats.say: A one million dollar bet, estimated at thirty. Against a reported fifteen million he turned down.
beats.visual: a staircase of glowing steps climbing into dark clouds, a single warm light at the top

beats.say: Now the honest catch. He was already one of the highest paid athletes alive, and he used his own cash.
beats.visual: a worn leather wallet open on a dark table next to an expensive wristwatch, moody low light

beats.say: Most people are never offered a stake, and plenty of equity deals pay nothing. We only hear about winners.
beats.visual: a long row of identical unmarked wooden doors in a concrete corridor, one slightly open with light, no people

beats.say: But the question travels. Next time you are paid for your work, ask what a piece of the result would be worth.
beats.visual: a pair of hands sliding a folded contract across a table toward a pen, late afternoon window light, no faces

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: a long empty road stretching toward a glowing sunrise horizon over a quiet city, wide shot

caption: LeBron James reportedly turned down $14-15 million from McDonald's and put about $1 million into Blaze Pizza. What ownership can do that a fee cannot, and the catch. Educational content, not financial advice.
description: Reportedly, LeBron James let a McDonald's endorsement lapse in 2015 and held equity in Blaze Pizza, which Forbes estimated at about $30 million in 2022. What it shows about fees versus ownership, and the honest catch.
first_comment: Would you take the guaranteed fee or a piece of the company? Educational only, not financial advice.

facts.claim: 2015 McDonald's endorsement not renewed; about $14-15M over four years per partner Maverick Carter
Early Blaze Pizza investor in 2012; about $1M first investment
Catch: among highest paid players, own money, many equity deals pay nothing
